title: Fixtures and fixture scope

overview.why: Without fixtures, you repeat setup code in every single test. Fixtures keep test files clean and ensure each test gets a fresh, predictable starting state.

why_learning_this: Reusing setup data across many tests without copy-pasting.
Speeding up tests by sharing heavy setup (like database connections) using session scope.

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting to request the fixture
common_mistakes.explanation: If your test function does not include the fixture name in its arguments (like `def test_name():`), pytest will not run the fixture and you cannot use its data.

common_mistakes.title: Mutating shared session fixtures
common_mistakes.explanation: If a fixture has `scope='session'` and one test changes the data, the next test gets the changed data. Only use session scope for read-only data.

recall_questions.q: Explain fixtures and fixture scope in your own words, as if to a classmate.
recall_questions.answer: A fixture is a setup function that runs before tests to provide data. Scope decides if it runs fresh for every test, or just once for all tests.

recall_questions.q: What is the default scope of a pytest fixture?
recall_questions.answer: The default scope is 'function', meaning it runs once for every test that requests it.

understanding_checks.question: What does test_two print?
understanding_checks.why: The default scope is 'function', so the fixture runs a second time before `test_two`, incrementing the global counter to 2.

understanding_checks.question: How many times does 'Connecting to DB' print when these tests run?
understanding_checks.why: Because the scope is 'session', pytest runs the fixture only once for the entire test run, and shares the result with both tests.

aha_moment.why: It prints 'Rahul'. The default scope is 'function', so pytest creates a completely fresh dictionary for `test_check`. The mutation in `test_change` is forgotten.

practice_tasks.title: Set the scope
practice_tasks.prompt: Given this code, change the fixture so it only runs once per test session.

challenge.title: Create and use a fixture
challenge.prompt: Create a fixture named `my_list` that returns `[1, 2]`. Then write a test function named `test_list` that requests the fixture and asserts its length is 2.
